default.notes: Group 2 nationality — a paid tourist visa, obtainable on arrival at a main airport or land border, or in advance at a consulate. Around USD 30 in clean cash US dollars; stays total up to 90 days per calendar year.

groups.notes: Group 1 nationality — no visa needed for tourism, up to 90 days within a calendar year. Entry stamps are often issued for 30 days and topped up free of charge at a migration office.
Group 3 nationality — a consulate can only issue a visa after prior authorisation from the Bolivian authorities. Allow several weeks to a couple of months and expect to name a host or sponsor.

BO.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Bolivian citizens.

US.notes: US citizens are Group 2 and pay a USD 160 reciprocity fee for a ten-year multiple-entry tourist visa, available on arrival or at a consulate. Each visit still counts toward a 90-day annual limit, and the fee must be paid in pristine cash US dollars.

IL.notes: Israeli passport holders have long been placed in Bolivia's restricted group requiring prior authorisation, and Bolivia severed diplomatic relations with Israel in 2023 — consular processing may be unavailable. Confirm the current position before making any plans.

CN.notes: Chinese citizens are treated as Group 2 and pay for a tourist visa, though Bolivia has periodically eased terms for Chinese tourists — confirm the current rule with a Bolivian consulate before booking.

TW.notes: Bolivia recognises the People's Republic of China and has no Taiwanese mission; Taiwanese passport holders should expect consular processing with prior authorisation. Confirm current handling before booking.

XK.notes: Bolivia does not recognise Kosovo, so Kosovan passports are not covered by the visa-free group — apply through a Bolivian consulate, and travel on a second nationality if you hold one.
